propositions: The epic-close bug screen's per-candidate broad exception handler degrades systematic LLM provider failures (e.g. Bedrock ValidationException on 32/32 calls) to 'unrelated' verdict C, silently blinding the caused_by bug floor with no signal in verdict, sidecar, or exit code.

LLMUnavailableError raised during completion verification must propagate and block the close (nonzero exit, ticket stays in_progress, no attestation) instead of degrading, consistent with absent-provider behavior.

The max_tokens re-clamp for smaller models was missing in review_kernel/verify.py:301, causing Bedrock 400s when a 128K model ceiling was carried into haiku 64K calls and never re-clamped (fixed in commit e49e7a418a).
Non-provider per-candidate screen failures must continue to degrade open (e.g. malformed output, store read errors) to preserve documented screen advisory semantics.

LLMUnavailableError must be re-raised at both seams (screen_candidates._row warm call and fan-out, run_screen advisory shield) to propagate to the close gate's fail-closed handler; the isinstance predicate includes LLMConfigError subclass by design.
